about: Drug classes that CARD's downloadable release omits but that published literature supports. Kept apart from CARD's own data so a rebuild from the downloads still reproduces CARD exactly, and every class added from here is marked as curated in the profile evidence. Issue #66; the gap was found by the spot check in docs/card-spot-check.md.

additions.reason: MRSA with an altered PBP2a (mecA) or PBP2c (mecC) is resistant to carbapenems as well as penicillins and cephalosporins.

citations.citation: Gajdacs M. The Continuing Threat of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Antibiotics (Basel). 2019;8(2):52.
citations.supports: Abstract: MRSA strains "are characterized by an altered penicillin-binding protein (PBP2a/c) and resistance to all penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems".

also_listed_by.note: Lists carbapenem for the PBP2-like family and for mecA and mecC. The CARD 4.0.2 download does not.

additions.reason: MRSA with an altered PBP2a/c is resistant to cephalosporins. CARD's download gives mecA this class but gives mecC only penicillin beta-lactam.

citations.citation: Gajdacs M. The Continuing Threat of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus. Antibiotics (Basel). 2019;8(2):52.
citations.supports: Abstract: MRSA strains "are characterized by an altered penicillin-binding protein (PBP2a/c) and resistance to all penicillins, cephalosporins, and carbapenems".

also_listed_by.note: Lists cephalosporin for mecC. The CARD 4.0.2 download does not.

not_added.reason: The CARD website lists monobactam for the PBP2-like family. No source found that supports it, and monobactams have no activity against Gram-positive bacteria, so there is no resistance to attribute to the gene.
mecB and mecD (the CARD website lists carbapenem, cephalosporin and monobactam for both). No citation found for these rarer genes, so they are left as CARD's download has them.
